what: The differentiable-engine doors (tangent, adjoint-test, sensitivity, param-grad): rows, door arguments, recorded check thresholds, the state fields and metrics a user can name. Data, not code: a new row (mesh, suite) or a new metric is a table entry.

thresholds.source: window DOT_F32 = 2e-5 (float32 window dot); Taylor: min |dJ / (h <x, g>) - 1| <= 1e-2 for a whole short forecast inside a resolved interval (err at the best h below err at the largest h); FD: the same forward differences against the tangent prediction <w, M x>; zero direction: 0 nonzero words

strict.what: the earlier bar, 0.84 of one single-precision rounding of the dot: --dot-bar strict

self_dot_bar.rounding: one rounding = 2^-23 (float32 epsilon) x max(|<y, M x>|, |<M^T y, x>|), both sums binary64 (the runner widens each float32 word before its product); the reading is (<M^T y, x> - <y, M x>) / one rounding, signed, so |reading| = rel_aligned / 2^-23
self_dot_bar.what: the whole-state dot's verdict (hexcore.dot_bar, and the runner's valid_derivative through AD_DOT_BAR): (a) every direction within 4 single-precision roundings of the dot (4.77e-07 relative); (b) over 8 or more directions (adjoint-test --dot-directions N) no one-signed drift: the mean reading within 2 standard errors of zero. The model and its derivative run in single precision, so a correct transpose cannot agree to better than about one rounding: the released build scored on the model's fields reads under half a rounding on 12 of 12 directions at 12 km and up to 1.18 at 3 km; the cumulus port's wrong rows read 128 to 705 roundings (fails a) and the 30-step 12 km window seven of eight directions positive (fails b). The gradient test against the real model is a separate check (taylor_best_err, 1 per cent)

thresholds.dot_rel_what: the float32 window dot of the objective's own direction (<w, M x> against <M^T w, x>); the program's bar is the whole-state dot's, in single-precision roundings of the dot (self_dot_bar)

once_per_plan.what: the whole-state check belongs to the operator (plan, runner, kernel set, card family, steps, row words, test direction), not to the objective: the first door on a key runs it and stores its verdict in the door's cache (<hex cache>/ad/checks, or GPUWM_HEX_AD_CHECKS); a later door named in reuse, on the same key, takes a stored passing verdict instead of running it again, prints one line saying so and names the verdict and the receipt of the run that made it in its own receipt; a door named in always runs it every time; a door named in neither runs it every time. A failed, unreadable or missing verdict is never taken, and any change of key runs the check again. --self-dot runs it; --no-self-dot claims no verdict

self_dot.direction: the runner's own seeded whole-state direction (--direction field, test direction 1): every state word of the start moved at once and the reverse seeded by the tangent result; it does not test the direction of any one objective

plant_error.what: --plant-error KERNEL:SCALE (default off): an error planted ON PURPOSE in one backward (adjoint) code, so a user can watch the transpose check catch a wrong derivative on their own card. The door hands the runner its test-only switch AD_PLANT on every window of the run (the bump, each direction, the whole-state dot); the runner reports what it planted in each window.json (planted_error: launches, words changed). The verdict line says PLANTED, never PASS or FAIL; the receipt is never valid and its answer check is never kept for later commands; the exit status is 4 when the check caught the error and 5 when it did not (or nothing was planted). Sensitivity refuses the option, and every door refuses the runner's planting words (AD_PLANT*) in its environment.
plant_error.side: reverse only: at every launch of the named code, the change its adjoint makes to one input's cotangent is scaled by SCALE (new = before + SCALE x (after - before), in binary64, rounded once to float32); the forward model, the recording and the tangent are untouched, so the tangent's own checks (fd, taylor, the bump against the real model) read as they do without it

directions.what: the test directions of adjoint-test, one window each on the same objective and step sizes: along each, the gradient's prediction is compared with the real model's change of the measure. One direction says little: a gradient can read right along a mid-level temperature bump and be wrong near the ground, and a direction along which the measure hardly changes tests nothing. --directions picks rows (a comma list, or all); a row's own default list is rows.<row>.adjoint_test_directions, else default. The first direction always runs: its window gives the dot, FD, Taylor and zero checks and the gradient the descent direction is made from. Each further direction costs one more window
directions.rule_what: a forecast is not smooth: a branch taken in one run and not in the other moves the measure by an amount that does not shrink with the step, so below some step size the difference quotient jumps from one step size to the next (the forecast's own roughness). A step size counts when it lies in a run of steady_steps neighbouring step sizes whose difference quotients agree within steady_within of the largest; its spread is the smallest such disagreement. A direction is inside the bar when, at a step size that counts, |ratio - 1| plus that step's spread is within bar (null: thresholds.taylor_best_err); outside when, at every step size of the steadiest run (the steady_steps neighbouring step sizes that agree best), |ratio - 1| less that run's spread is beyond it, so one step size at the measure's own noise floor does not undo it; otherwise unresolved (no step size counts: the measure changes less than the forecast's roughness along that direction; or the steadiest ones read within their spread of the bar). PASS: the first window's checks and the whole-state dot pass, every direction ran, no direction is outside, and at least min_resolved independent directions are resolved (two directions whose cosine is at or above independent_cosine count once). An unresolved direction is printed UNRESOLVED and never counts as a pass

bump.what: the potential-temperature bump of --at, --level, --amplitude, --radius-km and --level-width (perturbations.theta), in the first window; no draw

descent.what: minus the gradient itself: the first window's own gradient of this objective to theta and qv at fixed density and wind, each over its scale (size: 1 K, and a tenth of the local vapour), the largest word moved by one scale, on at most max_words words of the mesh (its largest). The direction a minimisation follows, and the one along which the measure changes most for its size; no draw

near-ground-moisture.what: water vapour only, on the seven lowest model levels: a smooth seeded pattern inside the bump's envelope, a tenth of the local vapour at its peak; temperature, density and wind fixed. Near the ground is where a term the linear model holds shows first

smooth-draw.what: a smooth seeded pattern on temperature and on vapour at every level inside the bump's envelope (1 K and a tenth of the local vapour at the peaks), each field its own pattern from the direction's one seed. A random direction often moves the measure by less than the forecast's roughness; it is then printed UNRESOLVED and does not count. On a large box it moves every cell and level inside the envelope: give --radius-km

The probe's roughness is a lower bound: a larger step flips more of the forecast's switches (on the 12 km updraft over 5 steps the bump's ratio moved 8 per cent at step 0.1 where the probe bound read 0.3 per cent), which is why the steady rule still applies

On the 12 km example the roughness of a storm measure moves the ratio by more than half the bar below a step of about 0.3, so its ladder keeps three sizes between 1 and 0.3 (1, 0.6, 0.3), the run of three a step size needs to count
